Subject: Azure/GCP listing policy QC and SLA alignment for Acme pilot

Hi all,

We have a pilot with Acme Analytics (related deal HUBSPOT-57891) and are preparing marketplace listings for both Azure and GCP. Before we go live with the published listing text and the support SLA language, I want to run a short compliance QC and confirm any platform-specific constraints on: branding, support-response SLA wording, and claims about data residency/encryption.

Action items I need help with from platform teams:
- Azure: Any prohibited phrasing around “enterprise-grade” / “SLA-backed” claims? Do you require specific support contact formatting or an Azure Marketplace support plan attachment?
- GCP: Any limits on using third-party logos or partner badges in listing descriptions? Preferred SLA phrasing for support hours and response times?

I've attached the current Azure listing draft (acme-azure-listing-draft.pdf) and a preliminary SLA matrix (gcp-sla-table.xlsx). Can you review and flag anything that would cause a policy rejection or require legal sign-off?

Target: get platform feedback by EOD Wed so we can move to publisher preview.

Thanks,

--
Diego Fernandez
Senior Partner Lead, Redwood Inference
diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

From: Azure Marketplace Team <azure-marketplace-team@microsoft.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure/GCP listing policy QC and SLA alignment for Acme pilot

Hi Diego,

Thanks for the note and the drafts — quick read below.

Branding/claims: Azure Marketplace policy is sensitive to third-party comparative claims (e.g., “faster than X”) and unverified security claims like “bank-grade” unless backed by an attestation. You can use “enterprise-ready” but we prefer neutral descriptors ("production-ready") unless you attach a security whitepaper. Avoid mentioning competitor names.

Support/SLA language: Marketplace requires a clear support contact and hours. You may state target response and resolution times, but we recommend qualifying language like "target response time" and providing an escalation path. If you want to represent an SLA term that's legally binding, you'll need a partner support plan attachment showing coverage. Our validation checks for a dedicated email/phone + documentation link.

Attachments: We can accept the current PDF but please add a short (1-page) support plan PDF. Also, on the listing page, replace the icon usage for Azure partner badge with the official SVG assets — do not embed an alternate logo.

I'll loop in the validation engineer if you'd like an expedited precheck (we can do a preview scan within 48 hours).

Regards,
Azure Marketplace Team
Marketplace Partner Support
azure-marketplace-team@microsoft.com

From: GCP Partner Relations <gcp-partner-relations@google.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure/GCP listing policy QC and SLA alignment for Acme pilot

Hi Diego — thanks for sharing. A few points from the GCP side: 

- Logos & badges: Use the GCP Partner badge assets (we'll provide a link). No third-party logos in the hero image; you can show customer logos only with written consent.
- Data residency: Don't claim "data stored in X region by default" unless the solution actually pins data; state the deployment options and recommended config.
- SLA wording: GCP prefers non-contractual "target" phrasing in marketplace listings. If the customer requires contractual SLAs, that must be surfaced through a contract and not the public listing.

If helpful, we can run the draft through our compliance checklist and return a marked-up doc. Availability: Thursday morning for a quick review call.

Best,
GCP Partner Relations
gcp-partner-relations@google.com

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2026 17:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure/GCP listing policy QC and SLA alignment for Acme pilot

Thanks — this is very helpful. Quick consolidation and proposed next steps: 

1) Branding: Replace any competitor claims and switch to "production-ready" descriptors. Use official Azure/GCP partner badge assets. Acme marketing has confirmed consent to publish their logo; I've attached the signed consent (see Drive link).

2) SLA language: We'll change listing copy to "target response time: <X hours>" and remove contractual-sounding phrases from the public listing. For customers that need contractual SLAs we will surface a support addendum in the contract (not the listing).

3) Attachments & validation: Azure asked for a one-page support plan PDF — we'll produce that by Wednesday morning. GCP offered a compliance checklist review on Thursday AM — let's take that slot.

4) Action owners:
- Diego: Push updated listing PDF and one-pager support plan to Drive by Wed 09:00 PT (done: acme-azure-listing-draft.pdf v1 attached).
- Laura: Confirm any legal sign-off on security claim language by Wed EOD.
- Alex: Coordinate the GCP checklist call Thurs 09:30 PT and invite Acme.
- Vanessa: Update the marketing hero with approved logos and share final assets.

Attachments included in this thread: acme-azure-listing-draft.pdf, gcp-sla-table.xlsx.

Diego

> 2) SLA language: We'll change listing copy to "target response time: <X hours>"...

Thanks, Diego — reviewed the draft for claims. A couple edits that matter: 
- Remove the phrase "fully managed secure enclave" unless Acme's deployment includes a documented HSM/KMS design. If they can provide an architecture note we can keep a toned-down "isolated compute option" line.
- Security claims: drop "SOC2-grade" unless we have a completed report to attach. You can say "undergoing SOC 2 audit" if true.

I'll provide written sign-off or requested edits by Wed EOD. If Acme can share the architecture note and the signed logo consent, we should be clear to proceed to preview.

Laura Bennett
